articles.title: Kremlin confirms trilateral Ukraine peace talks in Abu Dhabi next week
articles.description: MOSCOW, Nov 3 (Reuters) - Russia will hold three-way peace talks with Ukraine and the United States in Abu Dhabi from November 10-11, the Kremlin confirmed on Tuesday.Vladimir Medinsky, an aide to Russian President Vladimir Putin, will serve as Moscow's chief negotiator at the talks, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters on a conference call.US negotiators have been seeking a breakthrough in the war, now in its fifth year. The last US-mediated peace talks took place in February, before the United States and Israel launched a war against Iran.

articles.title: US to mediate trilateral talks with Ukraine, Russia in Abu Dhabi next week, US envoy says
articles.description: By Steve HollandWASHINGTON, Nov 2 (Reuters) - The United States will bring together delegations from Ukraine and Russia in Abu Dhabi on November 10-11 to discuss ending Moscow's war against Ukraine, post-war security agreements and de-escalation, US envoy Steve Witkoff said on Monday.US negotiators have been seeking a breakthrough in the long-running conflict before the winter sets in. The last US-mediated peace talks took place in February before the United States and Israel launched a war against Iran.

articles.title: Netanyahu pushes for new strikes on Iran, officials tell AP, and other Mideast news
articles.description: Officials tell The Associated Press that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu wants the Trump administration to carry out new strikes on Iran. They say that U.S. President Donald Trump has yet to commit to another round strikes. Iran says it has a two-day plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and resume nuclear talks with the U.S. if Washington meets its demands. Separately, Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthi rebels accused Saudi Arabia of striking a shipping port along Yemen’s Red Sea coast. Israel’s military said it was wrapping up a sweeping operation that began after a shooting in Hebron killed two soldiers.

articles.title: Oil slides on Hormuz deal hopes but Trump keeps Iran strikes on the table
articles.description: Oil prices fell on Monday morning as talks in Qatar revived hopes of reopening the Strait of Hormuz, but US President Donald Trump kept the threat of fresh strikes alive and Israel's Benjamin Netanyahu reportedly urged him to hit Iran straight after Tuesday's midterm elections.

articles.title: Doomsday Iran strike loading? Israel polls, US mid-terms and Trump's big dilemma
articles.description: US President Donald Trump faces mounting pressure to resume military operations against Iran after the November 3 midterm elections, with Israeli PM Benjamin Netanyahu pushing for fresh strikes as Qatar-mediated diplomatic efforts to revive negotiations continue.

articles.title: 'I Want To Be Nice': Trump Signals Possible Fresh US Strikes On Iran, Discusses Move With Israel's Netanyahu
articles.description: The remarks reportedly followed a Saturday phone call with Netanyahu on the state of US negotiations with Iran and how quickly to return to combat.

articles.title: 'Prepared to defend ourselves' if US attacks, says representative of Iran's Supreme Leader in India
articles.description: Iran's Supreme Leader's representative stated the country seeks peace but is prepared for conflict. Iranian officials responded strongly to recent threats from the United States and Israel regarding military actions. Both Iranian Defence Minister and Foreign Minister emphasized the need for direct negotiations concerning the Strait of Hormuz. The situation remains tense as military options are being evaluated in Washington.
